name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
description: NIST AI RMF overlay for AI agent deployments. Maps AKSI controls to the four core functions (GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, MANAGE) of the NIST AI RMF v1.0 (January 2023). This overlay is always-on for any AI agent deployment and satisfies AI RMF alignment claims made in the NIST RFI response (v9).
jurisdiction: US (voluntary framework, federal procurement increasingly expected)

reporting_obligations.assessment_type: AI trustworthiness evaluation across Govern, Map, Measure, Manage functions. No mandatory reporting cadence, but federal procurement increasingly requires AI RMF alignment documentation. Third-party AI assessors (3PAOs adapting for AI) may use this overlay for structured AI trustworthiness assessments.
reporting_obligations.reporting_entity: Organization deploying the AI agent; may also apply to upstream AI developers/providers where agent relies on third-party model infrastructure

human_oversight_mandates.basis: GOVERN 1.2 (accountability for decision-making assigned with appropriate human oversight), GOVERN 6.2 (processes for human-AI collaboration), MANAGE 4.1 (post-deployment oversight)
human_oversight_mandates.minimum_requirement: Documented human oversight configuration with accountable roles; decision-point logging; escalation path for AI-generated outputs exceeding risk tolerance

notes: NIST AI RMF v1.0 (January 2023) is a voluntary framework but increasingly referenced in federal procurement requirements and executive orders on AI. The framework uses four functions (GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, MANAGE) rather than NIST CSF's IDENTIFY/PROTECT/DETECT/RESPOND/RECOVER structure. GOVERN is foundational — without GOVERN controls (GOV-01 through GOV-04), the MAP/MEASURE/MANAGE functions cannot operate effectively. AKSI controls map most densely to MAP (context establishment and risk identification) and MEASURE (performance measurement and evaluation) functions. The MANAGE function maps to AKSI's RS and RC controls. This overlay is always-on because AI RMF applies to all AI system deployments regardless of data classification. Federal deployments should also reference NIST AI RMF Playbook and sector-specific profiles (NIST AI RMF Financial Services Profile, etc.) which may impose additional specificity.
